newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares recover, brokers see slow rally.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares recover, brokers see slow rally.

text.p: Egyptian share prices recovered across the board on Tuesday in what brokers said could be the start of a cautious rally from recent four-month lows.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 4.75 points or 1.4 percent to close at 355.56. Turnover was a modest 38.63 million pounds ($11.38 million).
CMA figures showed the rally was particularly strong in the cement and milling sectors, the traditional barometer of investor sentiment on the Egyptian exchange.

"The market is starting to hold well. For the past few weeks most of the recommendations have been buy and quarterly results are showing lucrative figures," said Neveen El Tahry, managing director of brokers Delta EAB.

Commercial International Bank/CIB, which fell last week on disappointment about an annual dividend of two pounds, recovered for the second straight day, closing 3.20 pounds up at 70.10. It was the most active share, accounting for almost 20 percent of the day's trade.

All the biggest cement companies saw strong demand translate into higher prices. Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA gained 0.59 to 71.00, Amriyah Cement added 0.94 to close at 82.99 and Egyptian Tora Portland closed 1.75 up at 89.00.
But in much lower volume, Alexandria Portland Cement slipped 0.50 to 66.00.

All the partially privatised milling companies rallied, led by Central and West Delta Flour Mills, which hit the five percent threshold for price changes in any one session. It closed 4.11 pounds up at 86.31.
Sentiment in the banking sector was more mixed but Egyptian American Bank rose in relatively heavy volume, closing five percent up at 133.71 pounds, from 127.35 on Monday.
Tahry said she expected the bullish mood to last but without the frenzy which took prices to recond highs in February.
"Most buyers have set limits," she said. "This is not going to be a quick rally... It's a better educated market and people are thinking about investing for the long term."
The index for openly traded firms rose strongly to 498.28 from 487.82 points on Monday and that for the rarely-traded "closed" firms increased to 259.91 from 257.46 points.
Out of 81 shares traded, 39 rose and 29 fell while 13 ended unchanged. The volume of trade in advancing shares was more than eight times that in declining shares.
